details: Both candidates require supplied judgments: the formula does not implement the case-specific assessment or the genuine single-family, reimbursement, profit-objective and ordinary-course qualifications in unit daa1876316641.u40.28601; fidelity of those supplied classifications is not established by these checks.
The source packet lists an unavailable dependency, missing.b8f9c69dd226e4db3f4557d7; its effect on the broader licensing analysis cannot be assessed from the supplied text.

Both candidates require externally supplied judgments; the executable conjunction does not itself assess the case-specific factors or single-family qualifications in u40, so fidelity of those assessments remains unverified.

Both extracted claims overstate the absence of guidance: u40 supplies case-specific considerations for “carrying on a business in Hong Kong,” although it supplies no exhaustive test or separate territorial rule.
Both candidates introduce uncertainty and conflict-handling conventions that the source does not prescribe; these are computational policies, not additional legal requirements.
The referenced missing dependency is unavailable, so these checks establish fidelity to the supplied source requirements only.

Both candidates implement only the conjunction of supplied classifications; they do not implement the regulated-activity carve-out or the case-specific business assessment, so fidelity of those upstream classifications remains unverified.
The first claim’s MUST/OBLIGATION metadata could misleadingly suggest a duty to satisfy the trigger; the source instead makes the three factors conditions for a licensing obligation.
The missing incorporated dependency limits conclusions about the wider licensing regime, but does not prevent verification of the selected three-factor trigger.
